proofs.doc: The shift is a ring isomorphism (R, fadd, ⊞) ≅ (R, +, ·): it carries both operations.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.multAdd_not_distrib_add
proofs.doc: Plain addition and mult-add do not form a ring: ⊞ does not distribute over +.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.mpow_multAdd
proofs.doc: (a ⊞ b)^⊞n = a^⊞n ⊞ b^⊞n: each power map is an endomorphism of mult-add.
proofs.statement: mpow (multAdd a b) n = multAdd (mpow a n) (mpow b n)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.mpow_mul
proofs.doc: (a^⊞m)^⊞n = a^⊞(m·n): composing power maps multiplies the exponents.
proofs.statement: mpow (mpow a m) n = mpow a (m * n)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tate_glue
proofs.doc: The glued point: q − 1 sits with 0, i.e. multiplying the lift by q changes nothing. (Stated as 1 + 0 multiplied by q equals 1 + a whenever 1 + a = q.)

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateRel_multAdd
proofs.doc: Mult-add respects the gluing on each side.
proofs.statement: tateRel q (multAdd a b) (multAdd a' b')

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_commMonoid
proofs.doc: The Tate quotient is a commutative monoid under mult-add.
proofs.statement: CommMonoidLaws (TateQ.op q) (TateQ.zero q) where comm x y

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_glued
proofs.doc: In the quotient the class of q − 1 is the identity.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.tateQ_inverse

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.slope_walls_mod5
proofs.doc: Walls of slope addition (a + b)/(1 − ab) are the roots of 1 + a². Mod 5 and 13 there are two (two-walled country, a split torus with p − 1 points); mod 3, 7, 11 none (turning country, a non-split torus with p + 1 points). Split exactly at p ≡ 1 mod 4.

proofs.name: AbstractAlgebra.multAdd_one_wall_mod7
proofs.doc: Mult-add mod p always has exactly one finite wall, −1 (the other wall is at infinity).

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_lift
proofs.doc: Under the lift the mult-add integral is a product integral.
proofs.statement: 1 + mint d n = liftProd d n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_step
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem, part 1: the last step of the integral is the integrand.
proofs.statement: mint d (n + 1) = multAdd (mint d n) (d n)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem, part 2: a path whose mult-add steps are d ends at its start ⊞ the integral of d.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_box
proofs.doc: The same in box form: the end box is the start box times every step.
proofs.statement: 1 + f n = (1 + f 0) * liftProd d n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_const
proofs.doc: Straight lines are exponentials: constant mult-add slope a gives a^(⊞n).
proofs.statement: mint (fun _ => a) n = mpow a n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_add
proofs.doc: The integral over two intervals joins by mult-add.
proofs.statement: mint d (a + b) = multAdd (mint d a) (mint (fun j => d (a + j)) b)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.product_rule_step
proofs.doc: Product rule = sum rule: if f steps by d and g steps by e, then f ⊞ g steps by d ⊞ e.
proofs.statement: multAdd (f (k + 1)) (g (k + 1)) = multAdd (multAdd (f k) (g k)) (multAdd (d k) (e k))

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mint_multAdd
proofs.doc: The integral of d ⊞ e is the integral of d ⊞ the integral of e.
proofs.statement: mint (fun k => multAdd (d k) (e k)) n = multAdd (mint d n) (mint e n)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mpow_mul
proofs.doc: Chain rule for blocks: n blocks of m equal steps is a power of a power.
proofs.statement: mpow a (m * n) = mpow (mpow a m) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.rate_product
proofs.doc: If F grows by the factor (1 + h·p) over a step of size h and G by (1 + h·q), then F·G grows by (1 + h·(p ⊞ₕ q)): relative rates combine by weighted mult-add with weight h. This is time-scale ⊕.
proofs.statement: F' * G' = (F * G) * (1 + h * wAdd h p q)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.rate_product_limit
proofs.doc: Weight 0 (step size 0) is ordinary calculus: rates just add.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_exp
proofs.doc: The time-scale exponential after n steps: 1 + h·p^(⊞ₕn) = (1 + h·p)ⁿ.
proofs.statement: 1 + h * wpow h p n = (1 + h * p) ^ n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_exp_mul
proofs.doc: e_p · e_q = e_(p ⊞ₕ q): the exponential turns weighted mult-add into ×.
proofs.statement: (1 + h * wpow h p n) * (1 + h * wpow h q n) = 1 + h * wpow h (wAdd h p q) n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.step_iff
proofs.doc: Ordinary slope = height × mult-add slope (the log-derivative rule f' = (1 + f)·r).
proofs.statement: f (k + 1) = multAdd (f k) (d k) ↔ diff f k = (1 + f k) * d k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.leibniz_corner
proofs.doc: Leibniz's rule with the corner kept: the box f·g grows by two strips and one corner square.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => f j * g j) k = diff f k * g k + f k * diff g k + diff f k * diff g k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.diff_multAdd
proofs.doc: The ordinary difference of f ⊞ g: two lifted strips and the corner.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => multAdd (f j) (g j)) k = diff f k * (1 + g k) + (1 + f k) * diff g k + diff f k * diff g k

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.diff_pow
proofs.doc: An exponential's slope is a times itself, exactly.
proofs.statement: diff (fun j => (1 + a) ^ j) n = a * (1 + a) ^ n

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_add
proofs.doc: The additive fundamental theorem: differences telescope.
proofs.statement: sumTo (diff f) n = f n - f 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.jackson_gap
proofs.doc: Stepping the input by mult-add moves it by h·(1 + x): the gap of Jackson's q-derivative with q = 1 + h, read in lifted coordinates.
proofs.statement: multAdd x h - x = h * (1 + x)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.mslope_step
proofs.doc: Away from the wall, the mult-add slope is the step: f(k) ⊞ slope = f(k+1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ftc_mslope
proofs.doc: Fundamental theorem with slopes read off: f(n) = f(0) ⊞ ∫ mslope f.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.ts_inverse
proofs.doc: Time-scale inverse ⊖p = −p/(1 + h·p): exists exactly off the wall.

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.dif_shift
proofs.doc: Shifting the input commutes with differencing.
proofs.statement: dif k (fun i => f (i + 1)) j = dif k f (j + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.dif_one
proofs.doc: Each difference at 1 is the difference at 0 plus the next difference.
proofs.statement: dif k f 1 = dif k f 0 + dif (k + 1) f 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.isum_add
proofs.statement: isum (fun k => g k + h k) m = isum g m + isum h m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.isum_congr
proofs.statement: isum g m = isum h m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.pascal_sum
proofs.doc: Pascal inside a weighted sum: the (n+1)-cube's layers split into two n-cubes.
proofs.statement: isum (fun k => (Cube.layer (n + 1) k : Int) * x k) (m + 1) = isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * x k) (m + 1) + isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * x (k + 1)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.newton
proofs.doc: Newton's forward formula: f(n) = Σ_{k ≤ n} layer(n,k) · Δᵏf(0).
proofs.statement: f n = isum (fun k => (Cube.layer n k : Int) * dif k f 0) (n + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.Calculus.cubes_example
proofs.doc: A worked check: the cubes 0, 1, 8, 27, … have third difference 6 and fourth difference 0, so Newton rebuilds n³ from the numbers 0, 1, 6, 6.
proofs.statement: dif 3 (fun j => (j : Int) ^ 3) 0 = 6 ∧ dif 4 (fun j => (j : Int) ^ 3) 0 = 0

proofs.name: FusedRate.ladder
proofs.doc: Ladder lemma: if each rung is the one below it run after one step of `s`, then rung j is the bottom rung run after j steps of `s`. On [1,2] the fused-linear rungs satisfy this with f x = b^x and s x = b^(x-1), which gives H_k(b,x) = b^(s^(k-3)(x)).
proofs.statement: ∀ j x, G j x = f (iter s j x)

proofs.name: FusedRate.grow
proofs.doc: Growth template: if each step multiplies the gap by at least p/q, then after j steps it is at least (p/q)^j times the start.
proofs.statement: ∀ j, p ^ j * d 0 ≤ q ^ j * d j

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.either

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.mpow_lift

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.half_is_identity

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.depth_useless

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.quarter_six

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.three_quorums

proofs.name: ConsensusFused.one_quorum

proofs.name: DarkSector.redshift_compose_int

proofs.name: DarkSector.lcdm_is_weighted_cube
proofs.doc: Flat ΛCDM, exactly: Ωm(1+z)³ + (1-Ωm) = 1 + Ωm·(z ⊕ z ⊕ z). The cosmological constant is the unit cube; matter is the weighted shell of the (1+z) cube around it.

proofs.statement: foldMA (xs ++ a :: b :: ys) = foldMA (xs ++ b :: a :: ys)

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.foldMA_split

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.scale_anywhere

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.additive_books_corner
proofs.doc: The additive breakdown PUE = 1 + PLF + CLF books the corner as cooling: CLF = c + p*c.
proofs.statement: it * (1 + p) * (1 + c) = it + it * p + (it * c + it * p * c)

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.loss_costs_one_plus_c
proofs.doc: One watt of electrical loss removed saves (1 + c) watts at the meter.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.unit_gap
proofs.doc: Exact gap: k(k+1)·[cost(k) − cost(k+1)] = c X² − k(k+1) a.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.add_unit_iff
proofs.doc: So add a unit exactly when X² passes (a/c)·k(k+1): the switch point is x*·√(k(k+1)), the geometric mean of k and k+1 in units of the sweet spot x* = √(a/c).

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.equal_share
proofs.doc: Equal sharing is best for a square loss: shifting d from one unit to the other costs 2d².

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.cube_layers
proofs.doc: Layers 1, 3, 3, 1 of the fused cube (1+d)³ − 1 = 3d + 3d² + d³.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.spread
proofs.doc: k fans each moving q: k·q³·k² = (k·q)³, i.e. total power = Q³/k² for total flow Q = k q.

proofs.name: DataCenterFused.spare_fan
proofs.doc: N+1 fans at speed N versus N fans at speed N+1 (same total flow N(N+1)): power ratio N² : (N+1)², so running the spare always helps.

proofs.name: DialSweep.scale3

proofs.doc: k = −1 is the characteristic polynomial at 1 (Fredholm's λ is −k).

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_top
proofs.doc: The top of the dial: det(I + kA) − k³·det A has only lower powers of k.
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul k x)) - k * k * k * M3.det x = 1 + k * M3.tr x + k * k * M3.e2 x

proofs.name: DialSweep.orth_neg_one

proofs.statement: M3.mul (M3.transpose (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) x))) (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) x)) = M3.add M3.one (M3.smul (-1) (M3.wmadd (-1) (M3.transpose x) x))

proofs.name: DialSweep.dialU_sq
proofs.statement: M2.mul (dialU k q) (dialU k q) = M2.sub (M2.smul k (dialU k q)) (M2.smul q M2.one)

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_product
proofs.doc: (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 − q·ab)·I + (a + b + k·ab)·U: the landscape law, lifted.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (dialU k q))) = M2.add (M2.smul (1 - q * a * b) M2.one) (M2.smul (a + b + k * a * b) (dialU k q))

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_det
proofs.doc: det(I + aU) = 1 + k·a + q·a², the landscape's wall polynomial.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) = 1 + k * a + q * a * a

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_det_eigen
proofs.doc: With eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂ (k = λ₁ + λ₂, q = λ₁λ₂) the walls are a = −1/λᵢ.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU (l1 + l2) (l1 * l2)))) = (1 + a * l1) * (1 + a * l2)

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_discriminant
proofs.doc: The three countries are the sign of the discriminant, the squared eigenvalue gap.

proofs.name: DialSweep.or_line
proofs.doc: The "or" line: a wall at certainty a = 1 exactly when 1 + k + q = 0.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul 1 (dialU k q))) = 1 + k + q

proofs.name: DialSweep.unitU_sq
proofs.statement: M2.mul (unitU κ) (unitU κ) = M2.smul κ M2.one

proofs.name: DialSweep.unit_product
proofs.doc: (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 + κ·ab)·I + (a + b)·U: projected, (a + b)/(1 + κ·ab).
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (unitU κ))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (unitU κ))) = M2.add (M2.smul (1 + κ * a * b) M2.one) (M2.smul (a + b) (unitU κ))

proofs.name: DialSweep.boost_walls
proofs.doc: κ = 1 (boosts): det(I + aU) = (1 − a)(1 + a), walls at the speed of light ±1.

proofs.name: DialSweep.rotation_no_wall
proofs.doc: κ = −1 (rotations): det(I + aU) = 1 + a², no real wall.

proofs.name: DialSweep.shear_is_add
proofs.doc: κ = 0 (shears): det(I + aU) = 1, and the law is plain addition.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (unitU 0))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (unitU 0))) = M2.add M2.one (M2.smul (a + b) (unitU 0))

proofs.name: DialSweep.kmadd_lift
proofs.statement: M2.add M2.one (M2.mul (kmadd kk x y) kk) = M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul x kk)) (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul y kk))

proofs.name: DialSweep.sylvester2
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul x kk)) = M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.mul kk x))

proofs.name: DialSweep.sylvester3
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.mul x kk)) = M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.mul kk x))

proofs.name: DialSweep.rank_one3
proofs.doc: A rank-one weight leaves no corner terms: det(I + u·vᵀ) = 1 + vᵀu.
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (outer3 u1 u2 u3 v1 v2 v3)) = 1 + (v1 * u1 + v2 * u2 + v3 * u3)

proofs.name: DialSweep.rank_one_dial3
proofs.doc: The matrix determinant lemma: det(I + A·u·vᵀ) = 1 + vᵀ·A·u.

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_charpoly2
proofs.doc: det(I + kA) = k²·p_A(−1/k) (2×2), for k ≠ 0.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k x)) = k * k * charpoly2 x (-1 / k)

proofs.name: DialSweep.det_charpoly3
proofs.statement: M3.det (M3.add M3.one (M3.smul k x)) = -(k * k * k) * charpoly3 x (-1 / k)

proofs.name: DialSweep.wall_iff_eigen2
proofs.doc: The matrix sits on the wall of weight k exactly when −1/k is an eigenvalue.
proofs.statement: M2.det (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k x)) = 0 ↔ charpoly2 x (-1 / k) = 0

proofs.name: DialSweep.dial_lens
proofs.doc: The landscape lens law comes out of the dial matrix: off the wall 1 − q·ab ≠ 0, (I + aU)(I + bU) = (1 − q·ab)·(I + cU) with c = (a + b + k·ab)/(1 − q·ab).
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul a (dialU k q))) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul b (dialU k q))) = M2.smul (1 - q * a * b) (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul ((a + b + k * a * b) / (1 - q * a * b)) (dialU k q)))

proofs.name: DialSweep.cayley_weighted
proofs.doc: The weighted Cayley transform (I + kS)⁻¹(I − kS) is the Cayley transform of k·s.
proofs.statement: M2.mul (M2.inv (M2.add M2.one (M2.smul k (M2.skew s)))) (M2.sub M2.one (M2.smul k (M2.skew s))) = M2.cayley (k * s)

proofs.name: DialSweep.winv
proofs.doc: The weighted inverse: off the weighted wall, a ⊞ₖ (−a/(1 + k·a)) = 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.fall_le_pow
proofs.statement: ∀ k, fall n k ≤ n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.layer_fact_le
proofs.doc: **The layer bound.** C(n,k)·k! ≤ nᵏ: distinct picks are at most all picks.
proofs.statement: layer n k * fact k ≤ n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.collisions
proofs.doc: **Collisions are few.** n·nᵏ ≤ n·fall n k + C(k,2)·nᵏ: the ordered picks that repeat an axis number at most C(k,2)·nᵏ⁻¹.
proofs.statement: ∀ k, k ≤ n → n * n ^ k ≤ n * fall n k + tri k * n ^ k

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.bernoulli
proofs.doc: **Bernoulli, with room to spare.** (c+1)^(k+2) + (k+1)(c+1)^k ≤ c^(k+2) + (k+2)(c+1)^(k+1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_nat_lt
proofs.doc: **The staircase climbs** (cleared of fractions): (n+1)^(2n+1) < nⁿ·(n+2)^(n+1) for n ≥ 1, i.e. (1+1/n)ⁿ < (1+1/(n+1))ⁿ⁺¹.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_add
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum (fun k => f k + g k) m = rsum f m + rsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_mul
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum (fun k => c * f k) m = c * rsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_shift
proofs.statement: ∀ m, rsum f (m + 1) = f 0 + rsum (fun k => f (k + 1)) m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_le
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → f k ≤ g k) → rsum f m ≤ rsum g m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_nonneg
proofs.statement: ∀ m, (∀ k, k < m → 0 ≤ f k) → 0 ≤ rsum f m

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.rsum_mono
proofs.doc: More nonnegative terms, bigger sum.
proofs.statement: rsum f m ≤ rsum f m'

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.binomial
proofs.doc: **The cube's corner count.** (1 + x)ⁿ = Σₖ C(n,k)·xᵏ.
proofs.statement: (1 + x) ^ n = rsum (fun k => (layer n k : Rat) * x ^ k) (n + 1)

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.wt_le
proofs.doc: **Each layer is at most 1/k!.** C(n,k)/nᵏ ≤ 1/k!.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.wt_ge
proofs.doc: **Each layer is at least 1/k! minus its collisions.** 1/k! ≤ C(n,k)/nᵏ + C(k,2)/(n·k!).
proofs.statement: 1 / (fact k : Rat) ≤ wt n k + (tri k : Rat) / ((n : Rat) * (fact k : Rat))

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.s_lt_three
proofs.doc: **The partial sums never reach 3.**

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.u_step
proofs.doc: **The upper partner only comes down.** u (N+1) ≤ u N for N ≥ 1.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_le_u
proofs.doc: **The ceiling.** Every step of the staircase sits under every u N.

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.s_le_stair
proofs.doc: **The floor.** For n ≥ N, the staircase is within 3·C(N,2)/n of s N.
proofs.statement: s N - 3 * (tri N : Rat) / (n : Rat) ≤ stair n

proofs.name: MultAdd.E.stair_lt_succ
proofs.doc: **The staircase climbs.** (1 + 1/n)ⁿ < (1 + 1/(n+1))ⁿ⁺¹ for n ≥ 1.

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.nonempty_subsets
proofs.doc: non-empty choices: a set of m things has 2^m − 1 non-empty subsets; joining two separate sets combines those counts by mult-add (pick from either, or both, but not nothing)
proofs.statement: multAdd ((2 : Int) ^ m - 1) ((2 : Int) ^ n - 1) = (2 : Int) ^ (m + n) - 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.product_error
proofs.doc: relative errors in a product combine by mult-add, exactly (the textbook rule "they add" is the k = 0 shadow that drops the corner e₁e₂)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.product_error_corner
proofs.doc: the corner that the first-order rule drops
proofs.statement: multAdd e1 e2 - (e1 + e2) = e1 * e2

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.constant_product
proofs.doc: if one factor of a constant product grows by a, the other must change by b with a ⊞ b = 0: the lever (weight × arm) and Boyle (pressure × volume) are the same picture
proofs.statement: (P * (1 + a)) * (V * (1 + b)) = P * V ↔ multAdd a b = 0

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.boyle_partner
proofs.doc: on a field the partner change is the mult-add inverse −a/(1 + a)

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.boyle_gain_loss
proofs.doc: pressure gains combine at k = +1 while the matching volume losses combine at k = −1: if (1 + a)(1 − d₁) = 1 and (1 + b)(1 − d₂) = 1 then the totals match the same way
proofs.statement: (1 + multAdd a b) * (1 - wAdd (-1) d1 d2) = 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.kepler_third
proofs.doc: T² ∝ a³ on percent changes: (1 + t)² = (1 + α)³ is t ⊞ t = α ⊞ α ⊞ α (the square's gnomon equals the cube's layers)
proofs.statement: (1 + t) * (1 + t) = (1 + α) * (1 + α) * (1 + α) ↔ multAdd t t = multAdd (multAdd α α) α

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.inverse_square
proofs.doc: gravity: when the distance grows by ρ the force changes by the mult-add inverse of ρ ⊞ ρ

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.cooling
proofs.doc: each step closes a fraction a of the temperature gap; after n steps the part closed is 1 − (1 − a)ⁿ, the union-of-failures power

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.lenses_in_contact
proofs.doc: two lenses in contact: powers add (the point (0, 0))

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.lenses_apart
proofs.doc: two lenses a distance d apart: total power P₁ + P₂ − d·P₁P₂, weighted mult-add at k = −d

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.squeeze_multiplies
proofs.doc: each lens's squeeze factor 1 − d·P (how much a parallel beam narrows over the gap) multiplies

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.field_lens
proofs.doc: the wall: a first lens that focuses exactly on the second (d·P₁ = 1) makes the second lens change nothing: the field lens of telescope eyepieces

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.parallel_is_inverted_addition
proofs.doc: parallel resistors (or springs in series, capacitors in series) are addition read through the inversion lens x ↦ 1/x: (RS/(R + S))·(1/R + 1/S) = 1

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_fib
proofs.doc: n sections ending in a short circuit give F(2n)/F(2n − 1): 1, 3/2, 8/5, 21/13, ...

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_walls
proofs.doc: the walls of one section are its fixed points: Z = (1 + 2Z)/(1 + Z) ⇔ Z² = Z + 1, the golden ratio and −1/golden ratio (two real walls)
proofs.statement: (2 * n + d) * d = n * (n + d) ↔ n * n = n * d + d * d

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.ladder_hyperbola
proofs.doc: every ladder value sits on the hyperbola n² − nd − d² = −1, which hugs the golden wall: so Z² − Z − 1 = −1/d² and the ladder walks into the wall
proofs.statement: (ladder k).1 * (ladder k).1 - (ladder k).1 * (ladder k).2 - (ladder k).2 * (ladder k).2 = -1

proofs.name: EllipticLead.node_param
proofs.doc: every line y = t·x through the double point meets the curve again at x = t² + a1 t − a2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.walls_are_branches
proofs.doc: the walls are the node's branches: with z = −1/t (so z·t = −1), t²·(1 + k z + q z²) − (t² + a1 t − a2) is a multiple of (z t + 1), with k = −a1, q = −a2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.slopes_factor
proofs.doc: the two tangent slopes m1, m2 factor the slope polynomial: a1 = −(m1+m2), a2 = −m1·m2, so k = m1 + m2 and q = m1·m2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.wall_poly_factor
proofs.doc: the wall polynomial in z factors through the branches: 1 + k z + q z² = (1 + m1 z)(1 + m2 z)

proofs.name: EllipticLead.slope_discriminant
proofs.doc: discriminant of the slopes equals the map's k² − 4q

proofs.name: EllipticLead.nodal_w
proofs.doc: the nodal curve's formal group: w = −1/y as a function of z is rational, w·(1 − a1 z − a2 z²) = z³ is the curve equation w = z³ + a1 z w + a2 z² w
proofs.statement: w = z * z * z + a1 * z * w + a2 * z * z * w

proofs.name: EllipticLead.tate_q0_law
proofs.doc: with z = 1 − v (v = 1/u, Tate's parameter inverted), the law z1 + z2 − z1 z2 is v1·v2

proofs.name: EllipticLead.tate_q0_is_multAdd
proofs.doc: and a = −z turns it into mult-add exactly

proofs.name: EllipticLead.d4_weight
proofs.statement: d4 (u * a1) (u * u * a2) (u * u * u * a3) (u * u * u * u * a4) = u * u * u * u * d4 a1 a2 a3 a4

proofs.name: EllipticLead.d5_weight
proofs.statement: d5 (u * a1) (u * u * a2) (u * u * u * a3) (u * u * u * u * a4) = u * u * u * u * u * d5 a1 a2 a3 a4

proofs.name: EllipticLead.multAdd_curve_d
proofs.doc: mult-add's own curve (a1 = −1, a2 = a3 = a4 = 0) has d_n = (−1)^n: the differential dz/(1+z), the log of mult-add, through layer 6

proofs.name: EllipticLead.ochanine_nodal_num
proofs.doc: Ochanine's elliptic genus at ε = δ² (the nodal case): numerator a√R(b) + b√R(a) with √R(x) = 1 − δx² equals (a + b)(1 − δab), so the law is (a + b)/(1 + δab): the signature at δ = 1

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_discriminant
proofs.doc: Frey curve y² = x(x − A)(x + B) = x³ + (B − A)x² − AB·x: 16 × discriminant of the cubic

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_c4
proofs.doc: c4 = b2² − 24 b4 with b2 = 4(B − A), b4 = −2AB

proofs.name: EllipticLead.frey_c4_at_A
proofs.doc: semistable: at a prime dividing A (A ≡ 0) c4/16 is B²; dividing A + B (B ≡ −A) it is A². Either is nonzero mod the prime when gcd(A, B) = 1, so the reduction is a node, never a cusp.

proofs.name: EllipticLead.euler_factor_walls
proofs.doc: Euler factors are wall polynomials: 1 − a T + p T² = (1 − αT)(1 − βT) when a = α + β, p = αβ

proofs.name: EllipticLead.hasse_turning
proofs.doc: Hasse (a² < 4p) puts the point (k, q) = (−a, p) in the turning country: k² − 4q < 0

proofs.name: EllipticLead.euler_units
proofs.doc: units: scaling T by λ moves (k, q) to (λk, λ²q), the landscape's units action
proofs.statement: 1 + k * (lam * T) + q * (lam * T) * (lam * T) = 1 + (lam * k) * T + (lam * lam * q) * T * T

proofs.name: EllipticLead.gap6_whole
proofs.doc: no other whole rung passes layer 6

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_11
proofs.doc: top-left entry: (1 + ka)(1 + kb) − q a b = D + k N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_12
proofs.doc: top-right entry: (1 + ka) b + a = N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_21
proofs.doc: bottom-left entry: −q a (1 + kb) − q b = −q N

proofs.name: EllipticS3.lift_22
proofs.doc: bottom-right entry: −q a b + 1 = D

proofs.name: EllipticS3.cayley_hamilton
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton for G: G² = kG − qI, entry by entry

proofs.name: EllipticS3.multAdd_is_1x1
proofs.doc: mult-add is the 1×1 case G = [1]: (1 + a)(1 + b) = 1 + (a ⊞ b)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.nonsplit_frob_is_inverse
proofs.doc: turning (non-split) torus: u^(p+1) = 1, so v = u^p satisfies v·u = 1 and the mult-add of v − 1 and u − 1 is 0: Frobenius sends the point to its mult-add inverse (a_p = −1)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.split_frob_fixes
proofs.doc: split torus: u^p = u, Frobenius fixes the lift (a_p = +1)

proofs.name: EllipticS3.quat_det_re
proofs.doc: det U: real part w² + x² + y² + z², imaginary part 0

proofs.name: EllipticS3.quat_discriminant
proofs.doc: trace U = 2w; its wall discriminant is −4 times the squared radius of its latitude 2-sphere: how deep a prime sits in the turning country is how big the sphere of rotations with its angle is

proofs.name: EllipticS3.middle_minus_neighbour
proofs.doc: middle layer minus its neighbour: 20 − 15 = 5 and 70 − 56 = 14

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.mul_bound
proofs.doc: |a·b| ≤ u whenever |a| ≤ u and |b| ≤ 1, written without `abs`.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.certainty_absorbs_iff
proofs.doc: Certainty swallows everything, a ⊕ₖ 1 = 1 for every a, exactly when k = −1. The statistics page's "or" laws are the line k + q_L = −1 of lens laws; the Tsallis laws have no denominator (q_L = 0), so they meet it only here.
proofs.statement: (∀ a : Rat, wAdd k a 1 = 1) ↔ k = -1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.escort_powers
proofs.doc: Raising every entry to a then to b is raising to a·b: escorts of escorts.
proofs.statement: (l.map (fun x => x ^ a)).map (fun y => y ^ b) = l.map (fun x => x ^ (a * b))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.lsum_div
proofs.statement: InfoFused.lsum (l.map (fun y => y / c)) = InfoFused.lsum l / c

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.div_pow'
proofs.statement: ∀ n : Nat, (x / c) ^ n = x ^ n / c ^ n

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.pow_ne_zero'
proofs.doc: Escort of an escort: P_b(P_a(p)) = P_{ab}(p), when the normalizers are nonzero.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.escort_escort
proofs.statement: escort b (escort a l) = escort (a * b) l

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_parseval
proofs.doc: Parseval on the tetrahedron: Σp² = (1 + |λ|²)/4.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.linear_entropy_choi
proofs.doc: The Choi state's linear entropy 1 − Σp² is (3 − |λ|²)/4: zero at the corners, largest (3/4) at the centre, constant on spheres about the centre.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.midsphere_iff
proofs.doc: Σp² ≤ ½ (collision entropy at least one bit) exactly inside the midsphere.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.edge_midpoint
proofs.doc: The edge midpoint (X with chance ½) is (1, 0, 0): on the cube's face, the sphere and the octahedron at once, with collision sum exactly ½.
proofs.statement: edgeMid.lx = 1 ∧ edgeMid.ly = 0 ∧ edgeMid.lz = 0 ∧ coll edgeMid = 1/2 ∧ len2 edgeMid = 1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.octahedron_in_ball
proofs.doc: Octahedron inside the ball: |x| + |y| + |z| ≤ 1 gives x² + y² + z² ≤ 1.
proofs.statement: x * x + y * y + z * z ≤ 1

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.ball_in_cube
proofs.doc: Ball inside the cube.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.compose_stays_in_ball
proofs.doc: Composition multiplies coordinates (QuantumNoise.comp_lx …), and a coordinate of a real channel lies in [−1, 1]. So composing never leaves the ball …
proofs.statement: (ax * bx) * (ax * bx) + (ay * b_y) * (ay * b_y) + (az * bz) * (az * bz) ≤ ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.compose_stays_in_octahedron
proofs.doc: … nor the octahedron …
proofs.statement: (ax * bx ≤ u ∧ -(ax * bx) ≤ u) ∧ (ay * b_y ≤ v ∧ -(ay * b_y) ≤ v) ∧ (az * bz ≤ w ∧ -(az * bz) ≤ w)

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_series
proofs.doc: Series: the collision sum of a composed channel, through Parseval.
proofs.statement: coll (p.comp q) = (1 + (p.lx * q.lx) * (p.lx * q.lx) + (p.ly * q.ly) * (p.ly * q.ly) + (p.lz * q.lz) * (p.lz * q.lz)) / 4

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.map_sq_outer
proofs.statement: (InfoFused.outer xs ys).map (fun t => t * t) = InfoFused.outer (xs.map (fun t => t * t)) (ys.map (fun t => t * t))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.collision_parallel
proofs.doc: Parallel (two qubits, independent faults): the 16 joint fault chances' collision sum is the product, so linear entropy composes by the union rule.
proofs.statement: InfoFused.lsum ((InfoFused.outer [p.i, p.x, p.y, p.z] [q.i, q.x, q.y, q.z]).map (fun t => t * t)) = coll p * coll q

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.depol_point
proofs.statement: (depol s).lx = 1 - 4/3 * s ∧ (depol s).ly = 1 - 4/3 * s ∧ (depol s).lz = 1 - 4/3 * s

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.diagonal_crossings
proofs.doc: Along the diagonal (λ, λ, λ) the octahedron's face is λ = 1/3 and the midsphere is λ² = 1/3, so the octahedron is strictly inside there.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.bit_collision
proofs.doc: One bit-flip channel's collision sum in the polarization λ = 1 − 2p.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.pattern_linear_entropy
proofs.doc: The n-fold fault pattern (a corner of the n-cube) has collision sum cⁿ, so its linear entropy climbs at weight −1: 1 − cⁿ = (1 − c)^{⊕₋₁ n}.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.cancellation_hides
proofs.doc: The net channel after n stacked flips is purer than its fault pattern: ((1 + x)/2)ⁿ ≤ (1 + xⁿ)/2 for x = λ² in [0, 1].

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.gap_two
proofs.doc: At n = 2 the purity gap is a perfect square.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.synd_antipodal
proofs.doc: Opposite corners give the same syndrome …
proofs.statement: ∀ a b c : Bool, synd (!a) (!b) (!c) = synd a b c

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.synd_diagonal
proofs.doc: … and corners with the same syndrome are equal or opposite: each syndrome is one body diagonal of the 3-cube.
proofs.statement: ∀ a b c d e f : Bool, synd a b c = synd d e f → (a = d ∧ b = e ∧ c = f) ∨ (a = !d ∧ b = !e ∧ c = !f)

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.syndromes_total
proofs.doc: No alarm: both ends of the main diagonal. Alarm: each of the three other diagonals.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.decoder_failure
proofs.doc: The vote picks the lighter end of each diagonal; the failures add up to the top two layers of the cube (QuantumNoise.maj3).

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.alarm_one_coin
proofs.doc: After an alarm, the leftover doubt is exactly one fresh coin of chance p.
proofs.statement: p * q * q / (p * q * q + p * p * q) = q

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.chain_rule_pair
proofs.doc: The chain rule on one diagonal, for any L with L(xy) = L(x) + L(y) (log is one): a·L(a) + b·L(b) = s·L(s) + [a·L(a/s) + b·L(b/s)] with s = a + b. Entropy of the faults = entropy of the syndrome + entropy left on the diagonal.
proofs.statement: a * L a + b * L b = (a + b) * L (a + b) + (a * L (a / (a + b)) + b * L (b / (a + b)))

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.nishimori_tanh
proofs.doc: On the Nishimori line e^{−2K} = w = p/(1 − p). Then tanh K = (1 − w)/(1 + w) = 1 − 2p.

proofs.name: EntropyNoise.kw_lens_polar

proofs.statement: norm 0 1 (mre 1 1 x 1 y) (mu 0 1 x 1 y) = norm 0 1 1 x * norm 0 1 1 y
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.euclid_triple_parts
proofs.doc: Euclid's triples: square the triangle q + p·i (mult-add power 2 in the complex lift)
proofs.statement: mre 1 q p q p = q * q - p * p ∧ mu 0 q p q p = 2 * p * q

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.angle_addition
proofs.doc: angle addition: (cos α + i sin α)(cos β + i sin β) at the complex point (0, 1)
proofs.statement: mre 1 c1 s1 c2 s2 = c1 * c2 - s1 * s2 ∧ mu 0 c1 s1 c2 s2 = c1 * s2 + s1 * c2

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.unit_circle_closed
proofs.doc: cos² + sin² = 1 survives angle addition: the unit circle is closed under the product

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.tangent_addition
proofs.doc: tangent addition is the landscape law at (0, 1): numerator x + y, denominator 1 − xy
proofs.statement: LandscapeMap.num 0 x y = x + y ∧ LandscapeMap.den 1 x y = 1 - x * y

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.double_angle
proofs.doc: double angle: (1 + x i)² = (1 − x²) + 2x·i, so tan 2θ = 2t/(1 − t²)
proofs.statement: mre 1 1 x 1 x = 1 - x * x ∧ mu 0 1 x 1 x = 2 * x

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triple_angle
proofs.doc: triple angle: (1 + x i)³ = (1 − 3x²) + (3x − x³)·i: the cube's layers 1, 3, 3, 1 land alternately on the real and the i axis, with the signs of i², i³
proofs.statement: mre 1 (mre 1 1 x 1 x) (mu 0 1 x 1 x) 1 x = 1 - 3 * (x * x) ∧ mu 0 (mre 1 1 x 1 x) (mu 0 1 x 1 x) 1 x = 3 * x - x * x * x

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.law_of_cosines_norm
proofs.doc: the law of cosines is the norm on the line q = 1, with k = −2 cos C: c² = a² + k·ab + b². At k = 0 it is Pythagoras.
proofs.statement: norm k 1 a b = a * a + k * a * b + b * b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.law_of_cosines_right_angle
proofs.statement: norm 0 1 a b = a * a + b * b
ambiguous: no move shows in its own text or in its compiled proof term, so only the statement gives its shape

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.flat_triangle_open
proofs.doc: on the border (k = ±2, angle 180° or 0°) the triangle is flat: c = a + b or c = a − b

proofs.name: SimpleLaws.triangle_lengths_real
proofs.doc: inside the turning country (k² ≤ 4) every side-squared is a true length, never negative

proofs.name: Infinities.evalL_addL
proofs.statement: ∀ p q : List Nat, evalL t (addL p q) = evalL t p + evalL t q

proofs.name: Infinities.wOnes_spec
proofs.statement: t * wOnes t n + 1 = (1 + t) ^ n

proofs.name: Infinities.cantor
proofs.statement: ∃ g : α → Bool, ∀ a, f a ≠ g

proofs.name: Infinities.half_iter_upper
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → g n ≤ h (h n)

proofs.name: Infinities.half_iter_lower
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → h (h n) ≤ g n

proofs.name: Infinities.half_not_poly
proofs.doc: If a half rung stayed under n^k, the whole rung would stay under n^(k·k). Since the whole rung (exponential) outgrows every polynomial, no half rung is polynomial.
proofs.statement: ∀ n, N ≤ n → g n ≤ n ^ (k * k)

proofs.name: InfoFused.climb
proofs.doc: K2, climb: the mult-add power climbs the cube.
proofs.statement: 1 + k * wpow k a n = pw (1 + k * a) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.linearize
proofs.doc: K4, linearize: any map that turns products into sums turns ⊕ₖ into + in the coordinate 1 + k·a. Taking L = log gives log(1 + k·a).
proofs.statement: L (1 + k * wAdd k a b) = L (1 + k * a) + L (1 + k * b)

proofs.name: InfoFused.lsum_append
proofs.statement: lsum (xs ++ ys) = lsum xs + lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.lsum_map
proofs.statement: lsum (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.outer_sum
proofs.doc: K5, outer sum: the grid's total is the product of the two edges.
proofs.statement: lsum (outer xs ys) = lsum xs * lsum ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.shan_append
proofs.statement: shan L (xs ++ ys) = shan L xs + shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.shan_map
proofs.statement: shan L (ys.map (fun y => x * y)) = x * lsum ys * L x + x * shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.outer_shan
proofs.doc: K6, outer log.
proofs.statement: shan L (outer xs ys) = lsum ys * shan L xs + lsum xs * shan L ys

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_rule
proofs.doc: Union rule for independent events: P(A or B) = p + q − pq = p ⊕₋₁ q.

proofs.name: InfoFused.survival
proofs.doc: Survival multiplies (K1 at k = −1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_is_flipped_madd
proofs.doc: The k = −1 rule is mult-add read on the negatives (K3).

proofs.name: InfoFused.incl_excl3
proofs.doc: Inclusion–exclusion for three independent events falls out of associativity: the signed corners of the mult-add cube.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-1) (wAdd (-1) p q) r = p + q + r - p*q - p*r - q*r + p*q*r

proofs.name: InfoFused.series_system
proofs.doc: A series system of n parts, each failing with chance p, fails with chance 1 − (1 − p)ⁿ (K2).
proofs.statement: wpow (-1) p n = 1 - pw (1 - p) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.hazards_add
proofs.doc: Survival multiplies, so cumulative hazard −log(1 − p) adds (K4).

proofs.name: InfoFused.union_grows
proofs.doc: Adding an independent part never lowers the chance of a failure.

proofs.name: InfoFused.hartley
proofs.doc: Hartley: typical-set sizes multiply, so bits add (log₂ of 2ᵐ·2ⁿ is m + n).
proofs.statement: pw (2 : Rat) (m + n) = pw (2 : Rat) m * pw (2 : Rat) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.shannon_additive
proofs.doc: Shannon additivity for independent sources, H(X,Y) = H(X) + H(Y), proved for any L with L(xy) = L(x) + L(y) and both distributions summing to 1.
proofs.statement: shan L (outer ps rs) = shan L ps + shan L rs

proofs.name: InfoFused.joint_sums_to_one
proofs.doc: The joint distribution of independent sources is a distribution (K5).

proofs.name: InfoFused.power_sums_multiply
proofs.doc: Power sums multiply. With xᵢ = pᵢ^q and yⱼ = rⱼ^q (and (pr)^q = p^q·r^q for real powers), this is Σ (pᵢrⱼ)^q = (Σ pᵢ^q)(Σ rⱼ^q) (K5).
proofs.statement: lsum (outer ws vs) = lsum ws * lsum vs

proofs.name: InfoFused.tsallis
proofs.doc: Tsallis pseudo-additivity, S_q(A,B) = S_A + S_B + (1 − q)·S_A·S_B. With k = 1 − q, Tsallis entropy is S = (P − 1)/k where P is the power sum. Stated with the k cleared: if k·S_A = P − 1, k·S_B = R − 1 and k·S_AB = P·R − 1, then k·S_AB = k·(S_A ⊕ₖ S_B).
proofs.statement: k * SAB = k * wAdd k SA SB

proofs.name: InfoFused.renyi_additive
proofs.doc: Rényi additivity: Rényi entropy is L(1 + k·S)/k, so it adds where Tsallis mult-adds (K1 + K4). Stated with the 1/k cleared.
proofs.statement: L (1 + k * wAdd k SA SB) = L (1 + k * SA) + L (1 + k * SB)

proofs.name: InfoFused.gini_simpson
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 2 (k = −1): Gini–Simpson G = 1 − Σp² is the chance two draws differ. Collision sums multiply, so G composes by the union rule: "the pair differs" = "A differs or B differs".

proofs.name: InfoFused.support_count
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 0 (k = 1): S₀ = N − 1, support sizes multiply, so N − 1 mult-adds: the N×M grid minus its unit corner.

proofs.name: InfoFused.shannon_weight
proofs.doc: Landmark q = 1 (k = 0): Shannon, plain addition.

proofs.name: InfoFused.uniform_tsallis_is_fused_power
proofs.doc: Rung 2: for N equally likely outcomes and k = 1 − q a whole number m, 1 + k·S = Nᵐ, so k·S is the fused power (N − 1)^⊕m (K2 with k = 1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.kraft_slack
proofs.doc: Kraft sums of two prefix codes multiply when you concatenate codewords (K5), and the slack 1 − K composes like failure chances (k = −1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.kraft_product
proofs.doc: The concatenated code still satisfies Kraft.

proofs.name: InfoFused.campbell
proofs.doc: Campbell's exponential cost: M = Σ pᵢ·D^(t·ℓᵢ) multiplies for concatenated independent sources (K5 on the weights), so M − 1 composes by plain mult-add.

proofs.name: InfoFused.lengths_add
proofs.doc: Expected length adds for concatenated codes (the k = 0 shadow of Campbell): Σᵢⱼ pᵢrⱼ(ℓᵢ + mⱼ) = Σ pℓ + Σ rm when both sum to 1. Stated on the grid sums.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_cascade
proofs.doc: Binary symmetric channel cascade: the off-diagonal entry of the product of [[1−p, p],[p, 1−p]] and [[1−q, q],[q, 1−q]] is p ⊕₋₂ q.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_polarization
proofs.doc: Polarization 1 − 2p multiplies along a cascade (K1 at k = −2).

proofs.name: InfoFused.piling_up
proofs.doc: Matsui's piling-up lemma: biases ε = 1/2 − p combine as 2·ε₁·ε₂.

proofs.name: InfoFused.n_flips
proofs.doc: n identical flips: 1 − 2·P(odd) = (1 − 2p)ⁿ (K2).
proofs.statement: 1 - 2 * wpow (-2) p n = pw (1 - 2 * p) n

proofs.name: InfoFused.qary_cascade
proofs.doc: The q-ary symmetric channel. An error moves a symbol to one of the other letters at random; a second error lands back on the right letter with chance c = 1/(alphabet − 1). Right after two hops: both right, or wrong then sent back. The error composes with weight k = −(1 + c).

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_never_cancel
proofs.doc: c = 0, letters never cancel (huge alphabet, or erasures): the union rule.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-(1 + 0)) e1 e2 = wAdd (-1) e1 e2

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_binary
proofs.doc: c = 1, two letters: a second wAdd_flip always undoes the first.
proofs.statement: wAdd (-(1 + 1)) e1 e2 = wAdd (-2) e1 e2

proofs.name: InfoFused.ladder_four
proofs.doc: c = 1/3, four letters: the depolarizing qubit channel's −4/3.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bec_capacity
proofs.doc: Binary erasure channel: erasures compose by the union rule and capacity 1 − e multiplies exactly.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bec_dpi
proofs.doc: BEC: capacity of the cascade ≤ capacity of each link.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_dpi
proofs.doc: BSC (crossovers taken ≤ 1/2): the cascade's crossover is at least each link's.

proofs.name: InfoFused.bsc_stays_below_half
proofs.doc: …and still ≤ 1/2, so it stays on the side where capacity 1 − h(p) falls as p rises. (That monotonicity is real analysis and is not checked here.)

proofs.name: InfoFused.sdpi_multiplies
proofs.doc: Strong data processing: the contraction coefficient (1 − 2p)² multiplies.

proofs.name: InfoFused.parallel_capacity
proofs.doc: Parallel channels: distinguishable messages multiply, capacities add (Hartley).
proofs.statement: pw (2 : Rat) (C1 + C2) = pw (2 : Rat) C1 * pw (2 : Rat) C2

proofs.name: InfoFused.parity3
proofs.doc: Parity of three noisy bits: the odd layers of the mult-add cube (1·3·3·1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.cube_corners
proofs.doc: Every corner of the cube {0,1}ⁿ: (1 + 1)ⁿ − 1 nonempty corners (K2 at k = 1, a = 1).

proofs.name: InfoFused.hamming_perfect
proofs.doc: Hamming codes are perfect: with n = m + r and n + 1 = 2ʳ, the 2ᵐ balls of radius 1 (a corner plus its n neighbours: layers 0 and 1) tile the n-cube.

proofs.name: InfoFused.check_node
proofs.doc: Check node: −2·(p ⊕₋₂ q) = (−2p) ⊕ (−2q), plain mult-add.
proofs.statement: -2 * wAdd (-2) p q = multAdd (-2 * p) (-2 * q)

proofs.name: InfoFused.variable_node
proofs.doc: Variable node: posterior odds multiply, so o − 1 mult-adds.

proofs.name: InfoFused.odds_to_velocity
proofs.doc: Odds product in ρ coordinates (ρ = (o−1)/(o+1)), with denominators cleared: numerator and denominator of the velocity sum.

proofs.name: InfoFused.velocity_corners
proofs.doc: Velocity addition lifts to mult-add on both corners: (1 + ab) + (a + b) = (1 + a)(1 + b) and (1 + ab) − (a + b) = (1 − a)(1 − b), so (1 + v)/(1 − v), the odds, multiplies.

proofs.name: InfoFused.vadd_assoc
proofs.statement: vadd (vadd x y) z = vadd x (vadd y z)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wmul_comm
proofs.statement: wmul k x y = wmul k y x

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wmul_assoc
proofs.statement: wmul k (wmul k x y) z = wmul k x (wmul k y z)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.eps_sq
proofs.doc: ε² = kε: the corner weight is the square of the infinitesimal.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.units_wAdd
proofs.doc: **Units multiply by weighted mult-add**: (1 + aε)(1 + bε) = 1 + (a ⊞ₖ b)ε.
proofs.statement: wmul k ⟨1, a⟩ ⟨1, b⟩ = ⟨1, wAdd k a b⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.units_multAdd
proofs.doc: With weight 1 the units multiply by plain mult-add.
proofs.statement: wmul 1 ⟨1, a⟩ ⟨1, b⟩ = ⟨1, multAdd a b⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.dual_units_add
proofs.doc: With weight 0 (dual numbers, 1-jets) the corner is dropped: relative slopes add. This is the logarithmic derivative of a product.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.twoPt_mul
proofs.doc: **The weighted dual numbers are two points.** Reading an element at x and at x + k turns the twisted product into the plain product at each point.
proofs.statement: twoPt k (wmul k x y) = ((twoPt k x).1 * (twoPt k y).1, (twoPt k x).2 * (twoPt k y).2)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.twoPt_weight_zero
proofs.doc: At weight 0 the two points coincide: the secant has become the tangent.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.diff_leibniz
proofs.doc: **Discrete Leibniz with the corner.** If f(x+h) = f₀ + h·f' and g(x+h) = g₀ + h·g', then (fg)(x+h) = f₀g₀ + h·(the ε-part of the product in R[ε]/(ε² − hε)). The forward difference of a product is that ε-part.
proofs.statement: (f₀ + h * f') * (g₀ + h * g') = f₀ * g₀ + h * (wmul h ⟨f₀, f'⟩ ⟨g₀, g'⟩).du

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.dual_inverse
proofs.doc: The dual numbers have no wall: 1 + aε always has the inverse 1 − aε.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.wall_no_inverse
proofs.doc: **The wall is a zero at the second point.** If 1 + ka = 0, the unit 1 + aε has no inverse in R[ε]/(ε² − kε): read at x + k, it is 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.off_wall_inverse
proofs.doc: Off the wall, the inverse is the weighted mult-add way back −a/(1 + ka).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.leibniz2
proofs.doc: The jet product is the product of functions: second-order Leibniz, (fg)'' = f''g + 2f'g' + fg'' (with f'' = 2·c2).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.jma_lift
proofs.doc: Mult-add of jets is multiplication through 1 + x, as everywhere else.
proofs.statement: jmul ⟨1 + x.c0, x.c1, x.c2⟩ ⟨1 + y.c0, y.c1, y.c2⟩ = ⟨1 + (jma x y).c0, (jma x y).c1, (jma x y).c2⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cube_depth_two
proofs.doc: **Jet order = cube depth.** Three relative 2-jets (no constant term) mult-add to their sum plus the three pair corners; the triple corner, which would sit at ε³, is gone.
proofs.statement: jma ⟨0, a₁, b₁⟩ (jma ⟨0, a₂, b₂⟩ ⟨0, a₃, b₃⟩) = ⟨0, a₁ + a₂ + a₃, (b₁ + b₂ + b₃) + (a₁ * a₂ + a₁ * a₃ + a₂ * a₃)⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cube_depth_one
proofs.doc: At order 1 only layer 1 survives: relative jets just add.
proofs.statement: wmul 0 (wmul 0 ⟨1, a₁⟩ ⟨1, a₂⟩) ⟨1, a₃⟩ = ⟨1, a₁ + a₂ + a₃⟩

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.nilpotent_inverse
proofs.doc: **No wall in jet space.** A relative jet ν has the finite way back −ν + ν² (the geometric series stops because ε³ = 0).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_one_add_smul
proofs.doc: **The volume change of a step is the mult-add cube.** det(I + h∇u) = 1 + h·P + h²·Q + h³·R.
proofs.statement: (X.step h).det = 1 + h * X.tr + h^2 * X.e2 + h^3 * X.det

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_diag_cube
proofs.doc: **In principal axes the step's volume change is literally mult-add:** det(I + h·diag(a,b,c)) = 1 + (ha ⊞ hb ⊞ hc).
proofs.statement: ((diag3 a b c).step h).det = 1 + multAdd (multAdd (h * a) (h * b)) (h * c)

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.diag_layers
proofs.doc: The layers of a diagonal gradient are the cube's layers of (a, b, c).
proofs.statement: (diag3 a b c).tr = a + b + c ∧ (diag3 a b c).e2 = a*b + a*c + b*c ∧ (diag3 a b c).det = a*b*c

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.cayley_hamilton
proofs.doc: Cayley–Hamilton, entrywise: X³ − P·X² + Q·X − R·I = 0.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_sq_traceless
proofs.doc: For an incompressible gradient, tr(X²) = −2Q.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_cube_traceless
proofs.doc: For an incompressible gradient, tr(X³) = 3R.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.e2_vorticity_strain
proofs.doc: **Layer 2 is rotation against strain.** For P = 0: 8Q = 2|ω|² − |T|², that is, Q = ¼|ω|² − ½|S|².

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_vorticity_strain
proofs.doc: **Layer 3, the far corner, is strain self-amplification plus vortex stretching.** For P = 0: 8R = det T + ω·Tω, that is, R = det S + ¼ ω·Sω.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_tr_cube
proofs.doc: For a symmetric traceless S (a pure strain), tr(S³) = 3·det S.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_e2_sumsq
proofs.doc: For a pure traceless strain, −2Q is the sum of the squares of its entries.
ambiguous: its statement could not be read, so its size is a guess

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sq_nonneg_int
proofs.doc: A square is never negative (core Lean has no ready-made lemma for it).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sym_e2_nonpos
proofs.doc: So on the integers (and likewise any ordered ring) Q ≤ 0 for a pure strain: the strain's second layer only ever dissipates.
proofs.statement: (⟨a, b, c, b, e, f, c, f, -a - e⟩ : M3 Int).e2 ≤ 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.e2_expand
proofs.doc: dE2 really is the first-order part of Q.
proofs.statement: (X.addS Y t).e2 = X.e2 + t * dE2 X Y + t^2 * Y.e2

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det_expand
proofs.doc: dDet really is the first-order part of det (the second-order part is dDet Y X).
proofs.statement: (X.addS Y t).det = X.det + t * dDet X Y + t^2 * dDet Y X + t^3 * Y.det

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_traceless
proofs.doc: The flow keeps the gradient incompressible.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_dQ
proofs.doc: **Layer 2 is driven by layer 3**: 3·dQ/dt = 9R (so dQ/dt = 3R).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_dR
proofs.doc: **Layer 3 is driven by layer 2 squared**: 3·dR/dt = −2Q² (so dR/dt = −⅔Q²).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re_conserved
proofs.doc: **The discriminant is conserved**: along restricted Euler, d/dt (27R² + 4Q³) = 54R·R' + 12Q²·Q' = 0. 27R² + 4Q³ is minus the discriminant of the cube polynomial λ³ + Qλ − R; its zero set is the Vieillefosse tail.
proofs.statement: 54 * X.det * dDet X (reStep X) + 12 * X.e2^2 * dE2 X (reStep X) = 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.det2_step
proofs.doc: The 2D step: det(I + hX) = 1 + h·P + h²·Q, the square (1, 2, 1).

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.tr_cube_2d
proofs.doc: In 2D an incompressible gradient has no third invariant: tr(X³) = 0.
proofs.statement: ((⟨a, b, c, -a⟩ : M2 R).mul ((⟨a, b, c, -a⟩ : M2 R).mul ⟨a, b, c, -a⟩)).tr = 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.re2_frozen
proofs.doc: **2D restricted Euler is frozen**: −2A² + tr(A²)·I = 0 for every traceless 2×2 gradient, so the self-advection is cancelled exactly by the pressure.

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.shift_is_corner
proofs.doc: The shift is the corner: S₁Δ₂v = Δ₂v + Δ₁Δ₂v (shift = 1 + Δ).
proofs.statement: d2 v (i + 1) j = d2 v i j + d1 (d2 v) i j

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.minor_is_divergence
proofs.doc: **The corner-kept minor is an exact discrete divergence:** minor = Δ₁(u·Δ₂v) − Δ₂(u·Δ₁v).
proofs.statement: minor u v i j = d1 (fun i j => u i j * d2 v i j) i j - d2 (fun i j => u i j * d1 v i j) i j

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_sub
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun k => f k - g k) n = sumTo f n - sumTo g n

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_telescope
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun k => G (k + 1) - G k) n = G n - G 0

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.sumTo_congr
proofs.statement: sumTo f n = sumTo g n

proofs.name: MultAdd.JetFields.box_minor_zero
proofs.doc: **The minor sums to zero over a periodic box**: the grid version of "∫ (layer 2 of ∇u) = 0" for a 2D map of the torus.
proofs.statement: sumTo (fun i => sumTo (fun j => minor u v i j) n) n = 0

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.num_comm
proofs.doc: commutativity, numerator and denominator separately
proofs.statement: num p a b = num p b a

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.den_comm
proofs.statement: den q a b = den q b a

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.num_zero
proofs.doc: identity: F(a, 0) = a / 1

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.assoc_num
proofs.doc: Associativity, projective form. Composing (a ⊕ b) ⊕ c with fractions N/D gives numerator N + c·D + p·N·c and denominator D − q·N·c; the other bracketing is symmetric. The two numerators are equal and the two denominators are equal, as polynomials.
proofs.statement: num p a b + c * den q a b + p * num p a b * c = a * den q b c + num p b c + p * a * num p b c

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.assoc_den
proofs.statement: den q a b - q * num p a b * c = den q b c - q * a * num p b c

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.inverse_num
proofs.doc: inverse: F(a, −a/(1 + p a)) = 0, cross-multiplied: the numerator vanishes

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_lift
proofs.doc: the lift, cross-multiplied: (D − u N)(1 − v a)(1 − v b) = (D − v N)(1 − u a)(1 − u b)
proofs.statement: (den (u * v) a b - u * num (-(u + v)) a b) * ((1 - v * a) * (1 - v * b)) = (den (u * v) a b - v * num (-(u + v)) a b) * ((1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b))

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_factor_u
proofs.doc: the lift actually factors: D − u N = (1 − u a)(1 − u b), and the same with v
proofs.statement: den (u * v) a b - u * num (-(u + v)) a b = (1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.lens_factor_v
proofs.statement: den (u * v) a b - v * num (-(u + v)) a b = (1 - v * a) * (1 - v * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.multadd_point
proofs.doc: mult-add is the point u = −1, v = 0: walls at −1 and at infinity
proofs.statement: num (-((-1) + 0)) a b = multAdd a b ∧ den ((-1) * 0) a b = 1

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.velocity_point
proofs.doc: velocity addition is u = 1, v = −1: walls at +1 and −1 (the speed of light)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.discriminant
proofs.doc: the parabola: the discriminant of the walls is (u − v)²

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parabola_additive
proofs.doc: the parabola itself (a double wall, u = v): the lens N(x) = x/(1 − u x) turns the law into addition. Cross-multiplied: N·(1 − u a)(1 − u b) = (a(1 − u b) + b(1 − u a))·(D − u N), with D − u N = (1 − u a)(1 − u b).

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parabola_den
proofs.statement: den (u * u) a b - u * num (-(u + u)) a b = (1 - u * a) * (1 - u * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.units_num
proofs.doc: rescaling by λ moves a point along a parabola through the origin: (p, q) ↦ (λ p, λ² q)
proofs.statement: num p (lam * a) (lam * b) = lam * num (lam * p) a b

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.units_den
proofs.statement: den q (lam * a) (lam * b) = den (lam * lam * q) a b

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.dial_is_multadd
proofs.doc: the dial: k·(a ⊕ₖ b) = (k a) ⊕ (k b); every k ≠ 0 on the straight line is mult-add in other units
proofs.statement: k * wAdd k a b = multAdd (k * a) (k * b)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.kdv_phase_shift
proofs.doc: the KdV soliton corner: A(f − 1) with f − 1 = e₁ + e₂ + A e₁e₂ is plain mult-add of A e₁ and A e₂ (each wave moved by its phase shift log A)
proofs.statement: A * wAdd A e1 e2 = multAdd (A * e1) (A * e2)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.rung_equivalent
proofs.doc: so the unit-free shape p²/(p² − 4q) of rung s is s: (4s)² = s·(16 s)

proofs.name: LandscapeMap.parity_reaches_floor
proofs.doc: at L = 2 (parity) the floor is reached exactly at full error: eigenvalue −1

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.lift
proofs.statement: add one (madd x y) = mul (add one x) (add one y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.wlift
proofs.statement: add one (smul k (wmadd k x y)) = mul (add one (smul k x)) (add one (smul k y))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.madd_assoc
proofs.statement: madd (madd x y) z = madd x (madd y z)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.wmadd_zero_weight
proofs.doc: At weight 0 the corner is gone: plain matrix addition.
proofs.statement: wmadd 0 x y = add x y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.det_one_add_smul
proofs.doc: det(I + kA) = 1 + k·tr A + k²·det A.
proofs.statement: det (add one (smul k x)) = 1 + k * tr x + k * k * det x

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.det_mul
proofs.statement: det (mul x y) = det x * det y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.tr_add
proofs.statement: tr (add x y) = tr x + tr y

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.Dk_hom
proofs.doc: The dial homomorphism, for every weight k at once (any commutative ring).
proofs.statement: Dk k (wmadd k x y) = wAdd k (Dk k x) (Dk k y)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.shifted_det_hom
proofs.doc: k = 1: the shifted determinant det(I + A) − 1 turns matrix ⊞ into scalar ⊞.
proofs.statement: det (add one (madd x y)) - 1 = multAdd (det (add one x) - 1) (det (add one y) - 1)

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.coupling_sets_weight
proofs.doc: det(I + M) − 1 = m₁₁ ⊞_w m₂₂ whenever m₁₂·m₂₁ = (1 − w)·m₁₁·m₂₂.
proofs.statement: det (add one m) - 1 = wAdd w m.a m.d

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.diagonal_is_multAdd
proofs.doc: No coupling (diagonal): mult-add, weight 1.
proofs.statement: det (add one ⟨p, 0, 0, q⟩) - 1 = multAdd p q

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rank_one_is_add
proofs.doc: Rank one (m₁₂m₂₁ = m₁₁m₂₂, determinant 0): plain addition, weight 0.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.madd_not_comm
proofs.doc: Two by two, a matrix never commutes for free: order matters for matrix ⊞.

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.orth_lift
proofs.statement: mul (transpose (add one (smul k x))) (add one (smul k x)) = add one (smul k (wmadd k (transpose x) x))

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rotation_condition
proofs.doc: For X = [[x, −y], [y, x]], Xᵀ ⊞ₖ X is (2x + k(x² + y²))·I.
proofs.statement: wmadd k (transpose ⟨x, -y, y, x⟩) ⟨x, -y, y, x⟩ = ⟨2 * x + k * (x * x + y * y), 0, 0, 2 * x + k * (x * x + y * y)⟩

proofs.name: LinearAlgebraMA.M2.rotation_condition_flat
proofs.doc: k = 0 drops the corner: the condition becomes Xᵀ + X = 0 (skew, the Lie algebra).
proofs.statement: wmadd 0 (transpose x) x = add (transpose x) x
